_directive: machine-facing SAT probe battery for surfacing unknown-unknowns; each probe is an OPERATOR that spawns a known_unknown CQ rather than enumerating an impossible list of unknowns.
purpose: Operationalize unknown-unknowns: instead of trying to enumerate what we do not know we do not know, run a fixed set of Structured Analytic Technique probes; each probe, applied to a topic, SPAWNS a new known_unknown competency question that is appended to the one CQ ledger (entry.spawned_by = probe_id).
reuse_note: argue ALREADY references Structured Analytic Techniques: 'Analysis of Competing Hypotheses' (ACH) and 'Key Assumptions Check' are covered by argue (claim_evidence_appraisal: defeater/scheme critical questions and unstated-assumption surfacing; competing-argument adjudication / IBE). Those two probes are owned_by 'argue' and are CITED/REUSED here, not reimplemented. Only the genuinely missing probes are owned_by 'new'.

probes.name: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses
probes.description: Enumerate the full set of plausible hypotheses and weigh each against ALL evidence by diagnosticity, rather than confirming a favored hypothesis. REUSED from argue (do not reimplement); B11 only records the spawned CQ.
probes.question_template: For topic '{topic}': which competing hypotheses best explain the evidence, and which item of evidence is most diagnostic in discriminating among them?

probes.name: Key Assumptions Check
probes.reuse_citation: argue.capabilities[charitable_standardization_and_enthymeme_supply], argue.capabilities[argument_reconstruction_and_warrant_backing] (unstated-assumption surfacing); argue grounds this in argue__argument_mapping.kb.json / argue__claim_evidence_appraisal.kb.json
probes.description: Make explicit the load-bearing assumptions the current view rests on and test which would, if false, overturn the conclusion. REUSED from argue (it already supplies + audits unstated/enthymematic premises); B11 only records the spawned CQ.
probes.question_template: For topic '{topic}': what unstated assumption is the current understanding most dependent on, and what evidence would confirm or break it?

probes.name: What-If Analysis
probes.description: Assume a surprising-but-possible outcome has already occurred and reason backward to the pathway that produced it, surfacing precursors nobody is currently tracking. ADDED by B11 (not present in argue).
probes.question_template: For topic '{topic}': if an unexpected outcome had already happened, what chain of events would have produced it, and which early precursor are we not yet tracking?

probes.name: Pre-Mortem Analysis
probes.description: Project forward to a stipulated failure of the current understanding and ask what we must have missed for that failure to be true, surfacing blind spots before they bite. ADDED by B11 (not present in argue).
probes.question_template: For topic '{topic}': suppose our current understanding turns out to be badly wrong; what overlooked factor would most plausibly explain the failure?

probes.name: Quality-of-Information Check
probes.description: Interrogate the provenance, currency, and independence of the evidence base itself (not the claim), surfacing where corroboration is illusory or sourcing is thin. ADDED by B11 (complements scholcomm CRAAP/SIFT and argue independence, but is run here as a probe that spawns a CQ).
probes.question_template: For topic '{topic}': which currently-believed claim rests on sources whose authority, recency, or independence is unverified and should be re-sourced?

probes.name: Indicators / Signposts
probes.description: Pre-specify observable indicators whose appearance would signal that the situation is changing, converting an unknown-unknown into a watched, falsifiable known_unknown. ADDED by B11 (not present in argue).
probes.question_template: For topic '{topic}': what observable indicator, if it appeared, would tell us our understanding is becoming outdated, and how would we detect it?
